protocol-core.plain: AWP is a two-layer network where RootNet controls registration and governance while WorkNets define concrete agent labor markets.
protocol-core.why: The workstation must understand this structure so it can hide protocol detail and expose only registration, selection, execution, and review actions.
protocol-core.caution: The key risks are recipient routing, value-action confirmation, and upstream skill changes that should not silently rewrite local behavior.

awp-skill.plain: awp-skill is AWP's official RootNet skill for registration, staking, allocation, WorkNet discovery, and core protocol reads and writes.
awp-skill.why: It is the workstation's main bridge to the official protocol surface and the dependency behind registration, qualification checks, and live queries.
awp-skill.caution: If the official skill changes upstream, protocol-core, registration flow, and risk boundaries must be reviewed together.

mine.plain: Mine is AWP's highest-priority data WorkNet, focused on discovering pages, scraping content, cleaning data, extracting structure, and submitting useful datasets.
mine.why: It usually lets miners start without stake, making it the safest long-running first workflow for new AWP users.
mine.loop: The default loop is URL and dataset discovery, deduplication, scraping, cleaning, structured extraction, submission, and keepalive.
mine.caution: Rewards depend on acceptance rate, duplication rate, IP decay, and quality gates at epoch settlement.

predict.plain: Predict is AWP's reasoning-based prediction WorkNet, where agents read market context and external signals before submitting direction, price, and sizing.
predict.why: It turns research quality into potential rewards, but only if duplicate reasoning, frequency, and risk are controlled.
predict.loop: The default loop is market context, signal gathering, judgment formation, order recommendation, monitoring, and review.
predict.caution: Predict is higher risk than Mine because wrong judgments, duplicate reasoning, and rate limits can directly damage results.

gov.plain: GovNet is a staged governance and trading WorkNet for reading public markets, voting, placing orders, tracking the current phase, and waiting for settlement.
gov.why: It represents judgment about WorkNet value and weekly emissions, so it can involve real value actions rather than pure observation.
gov.loop: The default loop is initialize, inspect phase, stake or allocate if needed, vote or observe, and wait for settlement.
gov.caution: Votes, orders, staking, and other irreversible actions must enter the confirmation queue before execution.

staking.plain: Staking locks AWP to mint veAWP and AWP Power for governance rights, qualification, and some WorkNet priority paths.
staking.why: It is an enhancement path, not a required first step for every new user.
staking.caution: Staking moves value and locks liquidity, so term, impact, and confirmation must be explicit.

dao.plain: DAO is AWP's governance surface for proposals, votes, and protocol direction changes.
dao.why: Users may not touch the DAO daily, but the workstation must understand it because staking, AWP Power, and GovNet connect to it.
dao.caution: Governance signatures and value-impacting votes are not pure observation; they require explicit confirmation.

ardi.plain: Ardi is a puzzle-style WorkNet with settlement windows where agents read prompts, choose high-confidence answers, commit, reveal, and inscribe.
ardi.why: It is event-driven rather than a continuous task loop.
ardi.loop: The default loop is read puzzle context, choose up to five answers, commit, wait for reveal, then inscribe.
ardi.caution: Missing the current phase or ignoring `_internal.next_command` is the main operational risk.

kya.plain: KYA is a one-off identity, verification, and delegation WorkNet for identity checks, recipient routing, and delegated staking.
kya.why: It does not usually run as a reward loop; it unlocks prerequisites for other workflows.
kya.loop: The default loop is check identity status, decide whether registration handoff or verification is needed, set recipient, and grant delegation if required.
kya.caution: Identity binding, recipient updates, and delegated staking all require clear signing and confirmation boundaries.

tmr.plain: TMR is an officially active but still thinly documented WorkNet; its canonical Base ID is `845300000013`, while the older pending predecessor `845300000008` can still appear in the live API.
tmr.why: The workstation should verify live ID, official skill URI, and source depth before treating it as runnable.
tmr.loop: First verify `845300000013 -> https://github.com/awp-worknet/tmr-skill`, then inspect whether the repo has more than LICENSE before installing or executing.
tmr.caution: `minStake: 0` is only a live metadata hint; as of 2026-05-22 the official repo still lacks README, SKILL.md, and runtime instructions.

community.plain: Community is an officially active but thinly documented WorkNet; its canonical Base ID is `845300000011`, while the older pending predecessor `845300000006` can still appear in the live API.
community.why: The workstation must distinguish the thin skill entry from the community hub and avoid treating either as a mature runtime contract.
community.loop: First verify `845300000011 -> https://github.com/awp-worknet/com-skill`, then separate hub material from runtime instructions and wait for stronger execution signals.
community.caution: `minStake: 0` is only a live metadata hint; as of 2026-05-22 the repo still has only LICENSE and `awp.community` looks more like a community surface than an execution spec.

awp-skill-ops.plain: This reference covers awp-skill's official control capabilities: registration, gasless relay, recipient binding, staking, allocation, and live protocol queries.
awp-skill-ops.why: The workstation can hide protocol detail because it catches this layer and translates it into registration, selection, and execution actions.
awp-skill-ops.caution: If awp-skill installation, endpoints, or relay behavior changes, registration assumptions and automation boundaries must be reviewed.

mine-aip.plain: This reference captures Mine's protocol definition as AWP's first data WorkNet, focused on scraping, cleaning, and submitting structured web data.
mine-aip.why: Use this AIP to confirm Mine reward rules, settlement rhythm, and stake boundaries.
mine-aip.caution: It defines protocol boundaries, not whether the local runtime is installed; execution still depends on workstation scanning and local status.

predict-aip.plain: This reference captures Predict's protocol definition, combining prediction judgment, rationale, and order behavior in one market workflow.
predict-aip.why: Use this AIP to confirm virtual chips, reward splits, and market timing.
predict-aip.caution: It defines market mechanics, not whether the local skill is ready; execution still needs official runtime and qualification checks.

predict-skill-facts.plain: This reference captures Predict's official runtime and live registration facts, including skill source, WorkNet ID, and predict-agent constraints.
predict-skill-facts.why: It is closer than the AIP to what should run today, so it is useful for installation, command, and qualification checks.
predict-skill-facts.caution: If the official skill or live mapping changed recently, reread this reference before running automation.

gov-skill-facts.plain: This reference captures Gov runtime constraints, including public market reads, private state, signed actions, and phase detection.
gov-skill-facts.why: Gov's hard part is separating read-only observation from signed or value-moving actions.
gov-skill-facts.caution: Votes, orders, staking, and other irreversible actions must be confirmed before execution.

ardi-skill-facts.plain: This reference captures Ardi runtime constraints, including preflight, gas, qualification, commit, reveal, and inscribe order.
ardi-skill-facts.why: Ardi is a time-windowed event workflow, so this reference is more execution-relevant than a generic overview.
ardi-skill-facts.caution: If the official next command changes, do not handcraft a shell flow; return to the ardi-agent path.

kya-skill-facts.plain: This reference captures KYA runtime constraints, including identity verification, recipient routing, and delegated staking prerequisites.
kya-skill-facts.why: KYA does not run as a long-term earning loop, but it can decide whether other workflows may continue.
kya-skill-facts.caution: Identity binding, recipient changes, and delegated staking require signing-boundary and confirmation review.

live-worknet-canonical.plain: This reference records official live WorkNet names, IDs, and skill-source mappings so the workstation can avoid connecting to the wrong network.
live-worknet-canonical.why: When docs, old pages, and local cache disagree, prefer this live mapping before choosing a WorkNet target.
live-worknet-canonical.caution: It is a live registry, not a full operator manual; skill-source changes still need deeper review in the relevant dossier.
